# AI Craft Pattern Generator

Turn a photo into a printable craft pattern. Three crafts from one
shared engine: cross stitch, bead art, and an embroidery template.

| Input | Output (cross stitch, 100 x 100, 14 DMC colors) |
|---|---|
| ![sample input](docs/images/sample-input.png) | ![first pattern](docs/first-pattern.png) |

A full sample PDF (cover, materials, thread list, 4 chart pages) is in
[docs/sample-pattern.pdf](docs/sample-pattern.pdf).

*The images are synthetic (generated by `scripts/make_test_images.py`).*

## The web app

```bash
pip install -e ".[api]"
python -m app.main            # http://127.0.0.1:7860  (set HOST and PORT to change)
```

| Desktop | Phone |
|---|---|
| ![desktop](docs/screenshots/desktop-2-result.png) | ![phone](docs/screenshots/phone-2-result.png) |

The UI lives at `/` and the REST API under `/api` (interactive docs at `/docs`). Both call the same
service layer, so they behave identically.

| Method | Endpoint | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/health`, `/api/crafts` | Status; the crafts that are available |
| POST | `/api/generate` | Multipart: `file` (the photo) and `settings` (JSON). Returns the pattern, thread inventory and finished size |
| POST | `/api/preview` | Pattern JSON in, PNG chart out |
| POST | `/api/export/pdf` | Pattern JSON plus `title`, `paper`, `style` in, PDF out |

```bash
curl -F file=@photo.jpg -F 'settings={"width":80,"colors":12}' http://127.0.0.1:7860/api/generate
```

Errors use plain status codes: 400 for an unusable image, 413 for an upload over 10 MB, 422 for
invalid settings or a pattern that would be too tall (the message says how to fix it).

`scripts/screenshot_ui.py` drives the real UI in headless Chromium and saves the screenshots above
(needs `pip install playwright && playwright install chromium`).

## Quick start

```bash
python -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate   # Windows: .venv\Scripts\activate
pip install -e ".[dev]"

python scripts/make_test_images.py            # synthetic images (no photos needed)
python -m app.cli data/test_images/synthetic/sunflower.png --level 3 --out pattern.png \
    --pdf pattern.pdf --title "Sunflower"
```

CLI options:

```
python -m app.cli PHOTO [--level 1-5] [--width N] [--colors N] [--fabric-count 11|14|16|18]
                        [--strands 1-6] [--cleanup 0-3] [--crop L,T,R,B]
                        [--out pattern.png] [--json out.json] [--cell 12] [--no-symbols]
                        [--pdf pattern.pdf] [--title TEXT] [--paper a4|letter]
                        [--pdf-style tint|mono]
```

`--level` is the complexity slider (1 = 40 stitches wide, 8 colors; 5 = 200 wide, 40 colors).
`--width`, `--colors` and `--cleanup` override the level. `--crop` takes fractions, e.g.
`0.1,0.1,0.9,0.8`. `--pdf-style mono` prints symbols on white (best for black-and-white printers);
`tint` puts them on a light tint of each thread color.

Example output:

```
PDF -> pattern.pdf
Pattern: 100 x 100 stitches, 14 colors
Finished size on 14-count: 18.1 x 18.1 cm (7.1 x 7.1 in)
Generated in 0.05s -> pattern.png

Sym DMC      Stitches  Skeins  Name
A   3755         2963       2  Baby Blue
...
```

## How it works

1. **Load and validate.** PNG, JPG and WebP only. Size and pixel limits, EXIF orientation applied,
   transparency flattened onto white, metadata dropped.
2. **Crop and downsample** to one pixel per stitch (area interpolation).
3. **Cluster** the distinct colors with k-means in CIELAB, weighted by pixel count.
4. **Match to real DMC threads** with CIEDE2000, merge clusters that land on the same thread,
   then re-assign every pixel to the nearest *chosen* thread.
5. **Clean up.** Regions smaller than a threshold (lone stitches up to 7-stitch islands, set by
   `--cleanup`) dissolve into the visually closest neighbouring color. Large regions are untouched.
6. **Assemble** a grid of palette indices, most-used thread first, with a unique symbol per thread.
7. **Derive everything else** from that grid: preview image, stitch counts, finished size, an
   approximate skein estimate and the PDF.

The PDF has a cover, a materials list, a thread list (symbol, swatch, DMC code, name, stitches,
approximate skeins) and a paginated chart. Chart pages hold a multiple of 10 rows and columns so
page edges fall on bold lines, show row and column numbers, point to the neighbouring pages, include
a page-position minimap and list only the colors used on that page.

The pattern is stored as data (a grid plus palette), never as an image, so the preview, the future
PDF and saved projects all come from one source of truth. See [docs/decisions.md](docs/decisions.md).

## Project layout

```
app/
  cli.py                      command-line entry point
  core/config.py              limits and paths
  schemas/                    Pydantic models: settings in, GridPatternResult out
  services/
    imaging/                  load/validate, crop, downsample, Lab color, k-means
    palettes/                 loads DMC / diamond / Perler palettes, precomputes Lab
    crafts/                   CraftGenerator protocol, cross_stitch, preview renderer, sizing
    pdf/                      ReportLab export (cross stitch; bead and embroidery sections later)
  api/ ui/ db/                FastAPI, Gradio, SQLite
data/palettes/                palette JSON (see ATTRIBUTION.md)
scripts/                      make_test_images.py, benchmark.py
tests/
docs/                         product brief, design decisions
```

## Development

```bash
ruff check . && ruff format --check .
pytest --cov=app
python scripts/benchmark.py        # fails if the engine exceeds its time budget
```

CI (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) runs lint, format check, tests and the benchmark.

Current benchmark on the synthetic set (load + generate + preview + PDF): typical 100 x 100 about
0.4 s, 200 x 200 about 2 s, worst case (random noise at max settings) about 4 s.

## Known limitations

- **Corrupt or unreadable uploads get Gradio's message, not ours.** Gradio's image widget rejects
  files Pillow cannot parse (corrupt files, an unconverted HEIC) before our code runs. Formats
  Pillow can read but we do not accept (such as GIF) get the friendly message, and the REST API
  always does. Fixing the rest means replacing the upload widget; revisit if testers hit it.
- **Preview zoom is Gradio's fullscreen view.** There is no pan, zoom or tap-a-stitch inspection
  yet. A custom canvas preview (the plan's Option B) would add it.
- **Web fonts need internet.** The UI asks for Atkinson Hyperlegible from Google Fonts and falls back
  to the system font when it cannot load it (the screenshots were taken offline, so they show the
  fallback).
- **The legend scrolls sideways on a 320 px screen.** It fits at 360 px and wider.
- **No rate limiting or retention rule yet** (Week 9). Generated PDFs are deleted after an hour, but
  uploads and per-session pattern state are only cleared when the server restarts.
- **Presets are lightly tuned.** The level presets (width, colors, cleanup strength) were checked
  on synthetic images plus a handful of real photos that looked fine in manual review. A proper
  tuning pass needs the 15 to 20 image test set from the plan.
- **Rare colors.** A color can survive with only a few stitches (the sample uses two threads for 4
  stitches each), which means buying a skein for almost nothing. A "merge colors below N stitches"
  option is the next quality improvement.
- **Skein estimate is a heuristic** (full stitches only, fixed waste factor). Calibrate it against a
  published thread calculator before showing it to users.
- **PDF page overlap.** Chart pages do not repeat rows or columns from neighbouring pages; they
  rely on absolute numbering and "continues" pointers instead.
- Thread colors are on-screen approximations. Buy by the DMC code, not by how it looks on screen.
